Advertisement View all journals Saved research Search Account Log in Content Explore content About the journal Publish with us Subscribe Sign up for alerts RSS feed nature nature water articles article Article Published: 12 October 2026 China’s centralized wastewater treatment system reaches efficiency limits in tackling water scarcity Jijie Shen ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0003-2535-5265 1 , 2 , 3 na1 , Lei Shen ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0003-4782-3779 1 , 2 , 3 na1 , Shuai Zhong ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0001-7529-454X 1 , 2 , 3 , Delong Li ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0003-1050-9794 1 , 2 , 3 , Ding Li ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-3727-5919 1 , 3 , Jinzhu Fang 4 & … Haonan Bai 5 Show authors Nature Water ( 2026 ) Cite this article Save article View saved research 601 Accesses 18 Altmetric Metrics details Abstract Centralized wastewater treatment systems (CWTSs) are increasingly expected to strengthen water security through reclaimed water reuse. Yet whether centralized expansion can simultaneously achieve cost recovery and reduce water stress remains unresolved. We assess the viability of CWTSs in China using an inventory of 10,826 wastewater treatment plants and data on wastewater generation, reuse demand and socioeconomic scenarios. Here we show that CWTS benefits are spatially bounded: only approximately 0.45 billion people live in areas where reclaimed water reuse can achieve cost recovery and reduce local water stress. Under prevailing fees of 0.9–1.1 Chinese yuan m − 3 , cost recovery requires plants to reach break-even scales of 6,793–49,744 m 3 per day. Projected urbanization does not substantially expand viable reuse opportunities, leaving 95–99% of prospective plants in unserved areas below break-even scale. Hybrid centralized–decentralized systems can meet national targets at 25–37% lower cost. These findings support a transition from purely centralized to coordinated hybrid systems in developing regions.
